messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 — Heliotrope (Private VPC, dedicated pool) reporting widespread egress failures. Model endpoints returning 502/503; DNS lookups for customer-managed domain failing. Affected backend: rp-dedicated-us-west-2-3; NLB in front of pool showing connection resets. Paging @Sara (oncall) @Mike (infra) @Jenny (netops) @Kevin (support). Please ack and start triage.
Sara (oncall): Acked. Joining bridge now. Setting up incident channel.
Mike (infra): Looking at infra metrics — worker-to-internet bytes dropped spike at 2024-10-18T14:12Z. ELB stats show high TCP resets. No autoscale activity.
Jenny (netops): Checking VPC config for Heliotrope. Pulling SGs/NACLs and route tables now.
Kevin (support): I just DMed Heliotrope CSM to ask if any network changes were made on their side. Also preparing customer-facing update.
Alex (eng): Observing 502s from router logs: upstream connect failure. Could be outbound blocked or NAT exhaustion.
Mike (infra): Running quick checks: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values=rp-dedicated-*` and `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-xxxxx` — looking for recent rule changes.
Jenny (netops): Found a suspicious SG change at 14:10Z in Heliotrope account: egress rules reduced from 0.0.0.0/0 to only customer CIDR. That would block calls to third-party DNS and some model infra. Tag shows change by their automation user.
Kevin (support): Heliotrope confirms they pushed a baseline-hardening script last night that tightened egress. They thought only internal services needed egress. They did not realize Redwood agent needs outbound to model endpoints and DNS.
Sara (oncall): Triage decision: temporary mitigation on our side to restore service while they revert. Options: 1) Add a permissive egress SG on our ENIs to allow 53/UDP and 443/TCP to 0.0.0.0/0 2) Route outbound from dedicated pool via our NAT in customer VPC (if present) 3) Ask customer to revert. Prefer 1) for fastest recovery.
Mike (infra): I'll apply a targeted SG override on the dedicated pool ENIs to allow outbound TCP 443 and UDP 53 to 0.0.0.0/0 for 30 minutes. Applying now.
DeployBot: Executing: `rb infra sg-authorize --eni rp-dedicated-us-west-2-3 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --temporary 30m`
Mike (infra): Done. Also added UDP 53 rule. Confirming propagation.
Jenny (netops): Quick connectivity test from a worker:```
# on worker
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 example.com
93.184.216.34
$ curl -sS https://example.com/ -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
200
```
Jenny (netops): DNS and HTTPS resolved from a worker now.
Alex (eng): Model endpoints showing successful connections, 2xx responses resumed. Error rate dropping toward baseline.
Kevin (support): Sent update to Heliotrope: temporary egress rule applied on Redwood side; request them to revert automation or add exceptions for Redwood service. Customer acknowledged and rolling back their hardening rule now.
Sara (oncall): Monitoring for 15 more minutes. If stable, we'll remove temporary rule and ask customer to confirm their change. Also record CC on config change to avoid recurrence.
Jenny (netops): While we watch, noticed NAT requests for ephemeral ports were fine; no sign of NAT exhaustion. Root cause = customer SG harden.
Mike (infra): Rolling back our temporary rule in 25m unless customer asks us to keep. I'll put an expiration and a tracking ticket.
DeployBot: Rule has expiry metadata: expires=1951234740 (30m).
Alex (eng): Small follow-up — add explicit allow to customer-managed DNS (UDP 53) and allow to model telemetry hosts. I'll open a short-runbook entry.
Kevin (support): Customer confirms revert at 14:26Z. They pushed a targeted exception for Redwood egress.
Jenny (netops): Re-run tests from workers: dig/curl still green. Routing looked stable as their change took effect.
Sara (oncall): Error rate back to normal for 10+ minutes. Removing temporary SG now to validate end-to-end with customer config in place.
Mike (infra): Removing temporary SG rule. Command: `rb infra sg-revoke --eni rp-dedicated-us-west-2-3 --rule-id tmp-allow-egress-1951234567` — done.
Jenny (netops): Post-remove tests: dig and curl succeed. Model endpoints 2xx. No regressions observed.
Kevin (support): Notified customer that we've removed our temp rule and validated their config. They asked for a short postmortem and a suggested exception list.
Sara (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Logging timeline and action items. Will convert to follow-up ticket for runbook + KB.
Alex (eng): Action items: 1) Add a KB for customers about required egress (DNS, model endpoints, telemetry). 2) Update onboarding template to call out egress exceptions. 3) Add detection alert: if outbound to DNS or model endpoints drops >50% for >1m, page netops.
Kevin (support): I'll own customer comms + PM for KB.
Sara (oncall): Final status: mitigated at 14:32Z, resolved at 14:41Z after verification. Closing thread but leaving follow-ups in ENG-OPS board. Great quick work everyone. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident P1 mitigated — recording incident as RESOLVED, creating post-incident ticket INC-1951234567 for runbook + KB.
